label: r3c1
name: Roll-concat, 3 epochs, 128 envs
hypothesis: Same network as r2c1. The recipe changes to ppo_epochs 3, n_envs 128 and 16 minibatches of 128 samples. That gives about 35% more environment steps (about 158k) and about 77 policy updates instead of 29, with about the same number of gradient steps as r2c1. r2c2's failed seed probably came from its large minibatches and halved gradient steps, which this avoids. Refuted if the 2-seed mean falls below about 0.5 or a seed collapses to DONE.
last_analysis: The target channels are shown rolled by X/2 along x. That explains why every agent without a fix collapsed to DONE in round 1. Concatenating a copy of the observation rolled by X/2 solved this. After that, the recipe mattered most. Going from r2c1 (0.59, 29 updates) to r3c1 (0.89, 77 updates of 2048 samples, 3 epochs, minibatches of 128) shows that more frequent updates help. r3c1's training success was still rising at the end of its budget. Running 2 epochs with 256-sample minibatches risked a collapsed seed (r2c2). Gamma 0.99 hurt (0.41). Row/column context did not help (0.57 vs 0.59). The layer-factored head beat the plain head under the same default recipe (0.75 vs 0.59). That gap is larger than the seed noise we have seen, and that head has not yet been tried with the better recipe. For this final round I am testing: (1) the layer head with r3c1's recipe; (2) r3c1 with twice as many smaller updates; (3) both changes together.
